thread:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Rapid KV prefix cache key growth detected in us-west-2 cluster. Metric: kv_prefix_key_count up 48x over 7m, mempressure on cache nodes, continuous-batch queue depth rising. Dashboard: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/d/kv/kv-prefix-growth

oncall-alex: Acked. Paging now. I'm on the bridge, grabbing logs + traces. @sam can you get a quick diff of prefixes being written?

sam: On it. Quick snapshot: keys started exploding ~2024-06-14T03:28Z after the templating deploy yesterday. Example key patterns (trimmed):
```
promptkey:user:template_v2:prompt_hash:3a7f9c...:tokens:0,1,2,...
promptkey:user:template_v1:prompt_hash:9b12ab...:tokens:0
promptkey:user:template_v2:prompt_hash:3a7f9c...:tokens:0,1
```
We see a lot of near-unique keys with tiny differences (whitespace/normalization/clitic changes). Cache writes per minute spiked from ~1200 -> 56k. 95p latency for generation climbed from 240ms -> 1.1s. Error budget breached.

maria: FWIW we pushed a tokenizer tweak in templating service yesterday (normalizeWhitespace + punctuation tweaks). Looks like hash for prefix keys is computed on post-template text using tokenizer tokenization output. If tokenization changes, same logical prompt gets new hash -> cardinality explosion. Continuous batching is then writing many small KV entries and never reusing them.

kevin: Suggested immediate mitigations: 1) disable prefix caching for templated prompts, 2) reduce continuous batching write window to limit writes, 3) evict the new noisy keys TTL sweep. I'll draft PR for quick config flip.

jensen: I'm running a targeted sweep to evict keys generated in the last hour that match the problematic pattern. Running:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://internal-cache.redwood/api/v1/evict" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CACHE_ADMIN" \ 
  -d '{"prefix_regex": "^promptkey:.*template_v2:.*","max_age_s":3600}'
```
Starting now. Expect ~30-40s of elevated IO during sweep.

oncall-alex: Good. While sweep runs, please push hotfix config: set PREFIX_CACHE_ENABLED=false for templated routes and set CONT_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=10 (was 50). That should stop new unique writes and reduce churn.

kevin: PR open: https://git.internal/redwood/configs/pulls/4827 -> patch sets FEATURE_PREFIX_CACHE_TEMPLATED=false and CONT_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=10 for us-west. Deploying to prod canary.

deploy-bot: Deploy started for config patch by kevin to cluster us-west-2. Canary: 10% traffic.

sam: Canary metrics at +5m: key write rate down 82% in canary hosts, write amplification reduced. No obvious errors in canary. Rolling to 100%.

deploy-bot: Deploy successful: config patch rolled to 100% in us-west-2.

jensen: Sweep finished. Evicted ~1.2M keys matching template_v2 pattern; reclaimed ~18GB across nodes. Post-sweep pressure dropping.

sam: Metrics update +20m: KV key count trending down, 95p latency back to ~300ms, error rate falling toward baseline. Continuous batch throughput down ~12% (expected).

lily: Customer-ops: We're preparing customer notices for top affected customers. Preliminary impact: ~14 customers saw increased latencies, 2 customers reported transient 5xxs for ~6-9 minutes. We'll follow up with case IDs.

oncall-alex: Root cause (summary): tokenizer change in templating pipeline altered token boundaries -> prefix hash function (which hashed token sequence) produced different values for effectively the same prompts. This created many near-unique keys; continuous batching wrote them, leading to write amplification and memory pressure.

oncall-alex: Immediate mitigation steps taken:
- Disabled prefix caching for templated routes (config flip)
- Reduced continuous-batch window to 10ms to reduce write coalescing pressure
- Ran targeted cache evict for v2 template key patterns
- Notified customers and created follow-up issues

oncall-alex: Follow-ups (handoff to kevin):
- Add tokenizer-stable-hash adapter that normalizes inputs pre-hash (strip/normalize whitespace, stable punctuation rules) -> owner: eng-ml (kevin)
- Add canary test in templating deploy pipeline that compares prefix-hash distributions vs baseline -> owner: devex (maria)
- Add alert for sudden prefix cardinality growth with automatic temporary throttling -> owner: eng-sre (jensen)
- Add telemetry to tag keys with template version and sampler id so we can safely sweep next time -> owner: platform (sam)

kevin: Taking follow-ups. I'll own the tokenizer adapter PR and add the canary check. Estimated ETA for adapter + tests: 5 business days. Will schedule rollback-safe rollout.

sam: Note for postmortem: we should consider making prefix hash versioned in keys (e.g., v1/v2) so we can detect and isolate flavor changes. Also consider a default prefix cache size cap per tenant to limit blast radius.

lily: I'll draft customer communication and coordinate with support for postmortem.

oncall-alex: Handing off to kevin for follow-ups and postmortem. I'll remain available if escalation needed. Incident mitigated and moving to post-incident review. Adding :thumbsup: reactions.

kevin: Acknowledge handoff. I'll create the follow-up tickets and ping owners.

inc-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. Incident id: INC-20240614-1832. Timeline saved to https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-20240614-1832

oncall-alex: Closing thread here. Thanks everyone for the quick response.
